(a) In General.—Any application process established under section 333 of the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012 (49 U.S.C. 40101 note) shall allow for a person to apply to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to operate an unmanned aircraft system, for purposes of conducting an activity described in subsection (b)—
        (1) beyond the visual line of sight of the individual operating the unmanned aircraft system; and 
        (2) during the day or at night.  
    (b) Activities Described.—The activities described in this subsection are—
        (1) activities for which manned aircraft may be used to comply with Federal, State, or local laws, including—
            (A) activities to ensure compliance with Federal or State regulatory, permit, or other requirements, including to conduct surveys associated with applications for permits for new pipeline or pipeline systems construction or maintenance or rehabilitation of existing pipelines or pipeline systems; and 
            (B) activities relating to ensuring compliance with—
                (i) parts 192 and 195 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations; and 
                (ii) the requirements of any Federal, State, or local governmental or regulatory body, or industry best practice, pertaining to the construction, ownership, operation, maintenance, repair, or replacement of covered facilities;   
        (2) activities to inspect, repair, construct, maintain, or protect covered facilities, including for the purpose of responding to a pipeline, pipeline system, or electric energy infrastructure incident; and 
        (3) activities in response to or in preparation for a natural disaster, manmade disaster, severe weather event, or other incident beyond the control of the applicant that may cause material damage to a covered facility.  
    (c) Definitions.—In this section, the following definitions apply:
        (1) Covered facility.—The term “covered facility” means—
            (A) a pipeline or pipeline system; 
            (B) an electric energy generation, transmission, or distribution facility (including a renewable electric energy facility); 
            (C) an oil or gas production, refining, or processing facility; or 
            (D) any other critical infrastructure facility.  
        (2) Critical infrastructure.—The term “critical infrastructure” has the meaning given that term in section 2339D of title 18, United States Code.  
    (d) Deadlines.—
        (1) Certification to congress.—Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a certification that a process has been established to facilitate applications for unmanned aircraft systems operations described in this section. 
        (2) Failure to meet certification deadline.—If the Administrator cannot provide a certification under paragraph (1), the Administrator, not later than 180 days after the deadline specified in paragraph (1), shall update the process under section 333 of the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012 (49 U.S.C. 40101 note) to facilitate applications for unmanned aircraft systems operations described in this section.  
    (e) Exemptions.—In addition to the operations described in this section, the Administrator may authorize, exempt, or otherwise allow other unmanned aircraft systems operations under section 333 of the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012 (49 U.S.C. 40101 note) that are conducted beyond the visual line of sight of the individual operating the unmanned aircraft system or during the day or at night.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that outside persons interacting with the FAA, plus the certification deadline, amount to participation. But the outside party's only role is applying for permission to operate, and applications for licenses or authorizations are excluded from the definition. The certification goes to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. Nothing in the section requires rulemaking, public comment, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or a right to sue.
fable.s: shall allow for a person to apply to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to operate an unmanned aircraft system

qwen_block.w: The section describes an application process for individuals to obtain authorization to operate unmanned aircraft systems. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses' from the scope of participation. The interaction is between an applicant and a federal agency for a permit/license, not a consultation or coordination with outside parties on a federal decision. The report to Congress is also internal government communication.
qwen_block.s: Any application process established under section 333 of the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012 (49 U.S.C. 40101 note) shall allow for a person to apply to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to operate an unmanned aircraft system
qwen_block.b:
1.  **Think briefly**: The section describes an "application process" for operating unmanned aircraft systems. It mentions that a person can "apply to the Administrator". It also mentions a "Certification to congress" and updating the process. The definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." and "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses - applying for something is not participating in the decision". The interaction described is an applicant submitting an application to a federal agency. This is a standard licensing/permitting process, not a participatory decision-making process like a public comment period, advisory board, or consultation with outside entities on policy. The report to Congress is internal government communication. Therefore, the label is "No".

opus.w: The outside parties here only apply for permission to operate drones. That is a license-style application, which the definition says is not participation. The other procedural step is a certification to congressional committees, and that stays inside the federal government. The section has no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation with states or tribes, or right to sue.

opus.b: The section might look like participation because outside parties (pipeline and energy operators) "apply to the Administrator," and the FAA must "submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a certification." Neither counts. An application for permission to operate is like a license application, which the definition excludes. A certification sent to Congress stays inside the federal government. Nothing here requires rulemaking, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body or consultation with outsiders.
